newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot propane plunges after quick rally.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot propane plunges after quick rally.

text.p: U.S. spot propane prices continued to plunge in brisk late trade on Wednesday following what one trader said was the world's shortest rally.
Spot prices in the both hubs shot up this morning following the release of the Energy Information Administration report registering scant inventory builds.
But values quickly turned south, pressured down by NYMEX crude oil futures and apparent attempts by some majors to push prices down ahead of incoming foreign cargoes.
NYMEX November crude oil futures also ended down 47 cents at $25.07 a barrel.
"Inventories are still pretty lean but people are looking at the petchems not cracking as much, imports coming in and crude falling," one Houston player added.
In the U.S. Gulf Coast, Mont Belvieu spot propane traded at 49.25 cents for TET, one cent below levels traded this morning.
Conway, Kansas, hub material dropped down to 49.50/49.75 cents after trading as high as 51.13 cents this morning.
The EIA report said U.S. inventories of propane climbed a modest 0.9 million barrels in September, to a 26-year low of 50.4 million barrels.
Inventories remained mixed regionally, falling nearly 900,000 in the Gulf Coast, but rising nearly 1 million in the East Coast and 500,000 in the Midwest.
-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1631
